text:
marta: Evening handoff — I'm swapping out. Quick watchlist after the synthetic traffic run in eu yesterday evening. Short version: prefetch noise on eu-encoder, KV eviction spikes ~19:12 UTC, router v2.3 saw transient 502s during run. Leaving notes + queries below. :wave:

watchdog-bot: synthetic-run `eu-loadtest-2026-03-17` finished at 2026-03-17T19:10:45Z. total_reqs=80234, errors=43 (0.05%), 99p_latency=1.2s

devon: Can you paste the alert ids and what to do if they fire? Also any dashboards to check quickly?

marta: Alerts: ENC_PREFETCH_HIGH (firing sporadically), KV_EVICTION_RATE_UP (brief spikes), ROUTER_502_RATE (transient). If ENC_PREFETCH_HIGH => check encoder-pool cpu and queue depth, don't page unless >5min sustained and 5%+ error rate. For KV_EVICTION_RATE_UP => check redis evictions, and if eviction rate >200/s for >2m escalate. ROUTER_502_RATE => verify model fallback is on; if routes >1% sustained for 3m, page eng-runtime.

lee: @devon @samira quick links: dashboard -> https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/enc/eu-encoder?orgId=1 , kv -> https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kv/redis-evictions , router -> https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/router/router-v2.3

samira: Can you paste the logs you saw? any obvious stack traces?

marta: log snippets: 
``` 
[19:12:07 UTC] encoder-eu-01 prefetch_queue=124 cpu=78% pref_threshold=100
[19:12:12 UTC] redis-eu-01 evictions=240/sec used_memory=78%
[19:12:14 UTC] router-v2.3-7f8c 502 upstream_timeout for /v1/generate seq=... 
``` 
No full trace, mostly upstream timeouts and queue pileups.

devon: Is this likely due to synthetic traffic only? any config we should tweak to reduce noise during future tests?

marta: Likely synthetic test plus slightly undersized encoder pool for the test burst. For next run: add small holdback by setting test -> rate_limit=0.8, and prefetch backoff: encoder.prefetch.backoff_ms=50 temporarily. I'll leave a script in /runbooks/synthetic/ if you need it. If you want I can schedule a short dry-run this morning.

watchdog-bot: note: scheduler detected test window overlap with peak backup job at 19:05 UTC — recommend avoiding 19:00-19:30 window for eu synthetic runs.

lee: I'll adjust the canary schedule for morning runs. If we see ENC_PREFETCH_HIGH again should we silence for the run?

marta: Yes — for controlled test windows: silence ENC_PREFETCH_HIGH and ROUTER_502_RATE using alertctl for the duration. Example: `alertctl silence --alert ENC_PREFETCH_HIGH --until 2026-03-18T03:00:00Z --reason 'synthetic run'` Keep KV_EVICTION_RATE_UP un-silenced; only silence if you have a redis engineer on call.

samira: Noted. Any followups I should do before taking over?

marta: Short checklist: 1) confirm silence scheduled if there's a planned test. 2) watch dashboards for 15m after test. 3) if KV eviction >200/s for >2m -> escalate to ops@redwood (pager). 4) file a short post-run note in #postmortems if run created >0.5% errors. I left a short runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.internal/runbooks/synthetic-load-eu

devon: Thanks — I'll run a 5m dry-run at 02:30 UTC and ping here. :eyes:

marta: Thanks team, leaving now. @lee please own morning check if anything lingers. :wave:

lee: Got it. Good handoff, enjoy the evening.
